characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: This lever designs and oversees non-production demonstrators to test a platform-neutral or fallback authentication path for Danish digital identity. It controls the scope, architecture, and assessment criteria of demonstration work, prioritizing methods such as FIDO2/WebAuthn, OpenID Connect, GrapheneOS, and browser-based fallbacks. Its objectives are to validate security, interoperability, and user experience while producing credible evidence to inform policy and procurement. Key success metrics include demonstrators built and validated, risk-reduction evidence, documented cost/timeline implications, and tangible inputs to phase deliverables and procurement language.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: By delivering concrete demonstrators, this lever strengthens Coalition Building Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy, providing credible material for policy and procurement discussions. It amplifies trust in platform-neutral concepts and gives the coalition tangible references to push for inclusive contract terms.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This approach can divert scarce resources and extend timelines, potentially conflicting with Policy Advocacy Strategy cadence and risking delays to policy proposals. If EU Standards Engagement Strategy timelines diverge from demonstrator milestones, it may hamper alignment with EU bodies, and strain Coalition Building Strategy when stakeholders seek broader, non-technical priorities.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: This lever focuses on policy advocacy to shape procurement decisions around Danish digital identity resilience, continuity, and supplier concentration. It coordinates the submission of policy proposals, stakeholder engagement plans, and messaging to influence AltID requirements and procurement language toward platform neutrality. It actively assesses regulatory risk, political capital, and coalition dynamics, aiming to embed neutrality principles within official policy and procurement documents. Success is measured by policy proposals submitted, formal responses secured, and greater likelihood of platform-neutral standards adoption.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever reinforces Coalition Building Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy by aligning messaging across stakeholders and anchoring policy goals in both national and EU contexts. It also leverages the Demonstrator findings from Technical Feasibility Strategy to strengthen procurement narratives.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This approach can slow outcomes if policy messaging becomes bogged down in stakeholder disagreements, potentially conflicting with Coalition Building Strategy cadence. It may also invite regulatory capture concerns from incumbents, complicating alignment with EU Standards Engagement Strategy timelines.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: This lever focuses on building a broad, diverse coalition across civil society, privacy advocates, academics, security experts, contingency-planning stakeholders, and supportive policymakers. It coordinates engagement, messaging, and alliance-building to mobilize support for platform-neutral and fallback authentication. It also manages tensions among stakeholders with differing priorities and ensures a shared narrative, governance, and decision gates. Key success metrics include breadth of stakeholders engaged, alignment on core messages, timely decision gates, and a stronger advocacy position in procurement dialogues.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever magnifies policy impact by supplying a broad, credible constituency for platform-neutral goals, aligning messages with Policy Advocacy Strategy and leveraging the demonstrator results from Technical Feasibility Strategy to strengthen procurement positions. It also helps manage internal conflicts by distributing influence across civil-society and academic stakeholders.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This broad coalition can slow decision-making and complicate messaging, risking misalignment with Policy Advocacy Strategy cadence and overwhelming the process. It may also constrain procurement timelines if coalition positions require concessions or extensive due diligence, potentially clashing with Procurement Influence Strategy's push for timely, clear contracting terms.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: This lever shapes how the project influences procurement language, contracting terms, and supplier diversity to accelerate platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication. It controls the drafting of procurement criteria, evaluation scoring, and risk-language around supplier concentration. Its objective is to embed platform-neutral access, credible fallback capabilities, and resilience into official documents, while limiting lock-in to a few vendors. Key metrics include updated AltID procurement clauses, demonstrated supplier diversity, reduced cycle times, and measurable reductions in dependence on Apple and Google.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Procurement Influence Strategy complements Policy Advocacy Strategy by converting policy aims into concrete contract language, and aligns with EU Standards Engagement Strategy to promote interoperable terms across Europe. It also reinforces Coalition Building Strategy by grounding stakeholder demands in auditable procurement criteria.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever can invite gaming or superficial scoring if criteria are too granular or misaligned with reality, risking regulatory capture by incumbents. It may also conflict with Technical Feasibility Strategy when cost or timelines undermine platform-neutral goals, and with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if divergent procurement terms hinder standardization efforts.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: This lever engages EU bodies, technical working groups, and standardization processes to align Danish digital identity efforts with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements (eIDAS2, NSIS). It coordinates input, monitors developments, and advocates for platform-neutral concepts and certified fallback mechanisms within the EU framework. It aims to reduce lock-in and improve interoperability across borders; success metrics include timely input to EU consultations, alignment of national proposals with EU standards, and inclusion of platform-neutral and fallback language in EU docs. It also interacts with procurement forces to ensure supplier neutrality is reflected in cross-border procurement language.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever reinforces Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy by anchoring platform-neutral objectives in EU standards and procurement terms, while also supporting Coalition Building Strategy with cross-border legitimacy and shared language for stakeholder outreach.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU-focused engagement can slow decision cycles and invite competing priorities, potentially conflicting with Policy Advocacy Strategy cadence. It may also dilute coalition messaging if EU standards diverge from national goals, creating friction with Coalition Building Strategy as stakeholders juggle international and domestic agendas.
